F1 required behaviour. (a) The in-flight guard is held until the underlying `$.http.fetch` promise SETTLES (resolves or rejects), not until the 2 s race resolves. (b) After 2 s with no answer the status line still shows `🔌 ADHD engine unreachable` and the up->down toast logic is unchanged (the existing test 'a hung engine times out instead of wedging the poll' must pass unmodified). (c) While a request is outstanding, no code path (60 s tick included) starts a second `$.http.fetch`. (d) When the outstanding request settles, polling resumes at the next tick and a healthy answer then restores the `ok` status (and the 'ADHD engine is back' toast if the engine was previously up). The late answer of the timed-out request is DISCARDED: never written to the view, never toasted, because it is stale. (e) No unhandled rejection: the promise that loses the race must have a rejection handler attached when it is created, so a late rejection never reaches the host. (f) No timer leak: the 2 s timer is cancelled whenever the fetch wins, and after `session.end` (any reason but `clear`) a late settle changes nothing: no status write, no toast, no new fetch. (g) Preserve: the helpers are top-level functions that take `$` and the state object as arguments (the engine's static reader follows `$` only through them), the never-surface try/catch policy, the single-GET-of-one-URL safety property, and every existing constant.

Known trade-off to record in a short code comment AND in the return (do not invent your own cancellation): the guard design means that if the host never settles an abandoned request, polling pauses and the status line stays `unreachable` until it does. The host's own network timeout is UNKNOWN. State this honestly; do not claim the orphaned request is cancelled, because it is not.

F6 required behaviour. In the `session.start` registration block, when `$.command.register` rejects for `pulse-focus`, `break` or `done`, show ONE toast per failed name with fixed text `dopemux-pulse: /<name> could not be registered` (interpolate only the literal command name, never error text). Registration of the remaining commands and the poll start must still happen. The toast call is itself wrapped so it can never surface. A small local helper at the top of the file is fine. If F6 needs more than that (restructuring hooks, new state, harness changes outside register.test.ts), STOP the F6 slice, leave F1 complete, and report F6 as NOT_RUN with the reason; F1 is the priority.
